title: From 1947 to Tomorrow: The Pakistan We Dream Of
deck: Beyond the corruption, criticism, and challenges we see, countless Pakistanis continue to serve this land with dedication. Now, it is our turn to carry that spirit forward and build the Pakistan we dream of.
author: Romaisa Ilyas 1st year MBBS student at BKMC
body: Pakistan! What comes to your mind the moment you hear the name “Pakistan”?

Many
 people—almost 99 out of every 100 Pakistanis—when you say something 
about Pakistan, whether in their homes, institutes, or social circles, 
immediately think of corruption, barbarism, nepotism, terrorism, hate, 
and everything that is corrupt: healthcare, education, government, 
police, army, and even the people.

I don't know why. Why do people 
think about Pakistan like that? Why is hate spreading everywhere, 
especially among the younger generation—among us?

We, the younger 
generation, didn't see all of that. What we have studied from childhood 
until now is that Pakistan came into existence in 1947, on the 14th of 
August, through the continuous hard work of Mr. Jinnah and Allama 
Muhammad Iqbal. Since its establishment, it has faced many problems. It 
was not initially in a strong position as an independent country, yet it
 was entrusted to the hands of many great leaders, presidents, and prime
 ministers.

But the question is: why, after 79 years of its 
formation, is it still fixed in our minds that Pakistan is about to 
collapse and that everything has been eaten away by those in authority?

Yet,
 until today, this country is standing tall. It has value at the 
international level and has maintained its structure through countless 
ups and downs and conspiracies. Why? What is the secret?

The secret 
is that if we can criticize our country in a negative way, we can also 
pay tribute to the patriotic people of this nation who are secretly 
working day and night. They are silently contributing and together 
maintaining the name, honour, establishment, management, and governance 
of this country.

On this special day, 14th August 2026, we salute 
those souls in every field and every profession of this country—whether 
they are old people who have already done their part in serving this 
country, adults and teenagers who are still working and offering their 
share of service, or students who are the Shaheens of Iqbal, soaring 
high and seeking new skills and knowledge to make this country better.

And
 last but not least, the zeal and zest of our children, whose only 
slogan of “Pakistan Zindabad!” sparks the stars of hope for this 
country. One day, InshaAllah, our country will rank No. 1 among the 
nations of the world.

We were born here. We have drunk and tasted the
 water and salt of this country. We have breathed the air of this land. 
Everything we have today is, in one way or another, connected to this 
country.

Therefore, now it is our turn. It is our obligation to this 
land that we will never tolerate any harm or wound to our country. We 
will work hard, and we will build a new, developed, and prosperous 
Pakistan. We will offer our share of service to this country, no matter 
what others do with it. And we will never tolerate those hands that are 
trying to break apart this nation.
Pakistan Zindabad! Proud to be Pakistani!
